title: The Monty Tech assessment — the school bill nobody in Lunenburg votes on
points: 1. Lunenburg paid Montachusett Regional Vocational Technical $1,334,521 in FY2026, and 95.2% of that was a figure the state calculated. | 2. The required minimum contribution is not apportioned among member towns by their enrollment. | 3. So a Lunenburg child moving to Monty Tech does not raise the town's obligation. | 4. A Monty Tech pupil carries about half again the foundation budget of a Lunenburg one, which is why the money share runs well ahead of the head share. | 5. The town's own five-year forecast of this line missed FY2026 by $329,057. | 6. What the town is billed is not what the district spends, and the gap is Chapter 70. | 7. Monty Tech is the larger of the two routes out of Lunenburg's own schools, and it is not a departure. | 8. Eleven of the twelve figures the annual town reports give for this line fail the extractor's own reconciliation, and they should be read as candidates.
point_1: 1. Lunenburg paid Montachusett Regional Vocational Technical $1,334,521 in FY2026, and 95.2% of that was a figure the state calculated.

point_3: 3. So a Lunenburg child moving to Monty Tech does not raise the town's obligation.
point_4: 4. A Monty Tech pupil carries about half again the foundation budget of a Lunenburg one, which is why the money share runs well ahead of the head share.
point_5: 5. The town's own five-year forecast of this line missed FY2026 by $329,057.
point_6: 6. What the town is billed is not what the district spends, and the gap is Chapter 70.

point_8: 8. Eleven of the twelve figures the annual town reports give for this line fail the extractor's own reconciliation, and they should be read as candidates.

title: What comparable districts actually cut, and in what order

Lunenburg is in the bottom quarter of Massachusetts districts by total per-pupil spending, and it has been in every one of the seventeen years the state publishes. | 3. Against five neighbouring districts it has never been higher than fifth of six. | 4. Most of the spread between these six districts is the denominator, not the money. | 5. The gap is not spread evenly across the budget. | 6. Against the whole state the two smallest lines are the extreme ones. | 7. Lunenburg pays near the top of this set for teachers and employs the fewest of them per pupil. | 8. A tenth of what DESE counts as Lunenburg's school spending is not general-fund money, and that is the smallest share in the set. | 9. The two Chapter 70 standings that look like a contradiction are not one.
point_1: 1. 145 of the 177 Lunenburg children educated outside Lunenburg Public Schools go to districts that spend more for each pupil than Lunenburg does — 12.0% more at Leominster, and 43.3% more at Montachusett Regional Vocational Technical.
point_2: The set is every district that took 5 or more Lunenburg children in FY2026, derived from DESE's residents-sending and enrolment-receiving files rather than chosen; a further 16 children went to 9 other districts in ones and twos.
point_3: And nothing in this section is a foundation budget.
point_4: 2. Lunenburg is in the bottom quarter of Massachusetts districts by total per-pupil spending, and it has been in every one of the seventeen years the state publishes.
point_5: 3. Against five neighbouring districts it has never been higher than fifth of six.
point_6: 4. Most of the spread between these six districts is the denominator, not the money.
point_7: 5. The gap is not spread evenly across the budget.
point_8: 6. Against the whole state the two smallest lines are the extreme ones.
point_9: 7. Lunenburg pays near the top of this set for teachers and employs the fewest of them per pupil.
point_10: 8. A tenth of what DESE counts as Lunenburg's school spending is not general-fund money, and that is the smallest share in the set.
point_11: 9. The two Chapter 70 standings that look like a contradiction are not one.
